The [Chang'e 5](/wiki/Chang%27e_5 "Chang'e 5") returner carrying a lunar sample was transported back to [CAST](/wiki/China_Academy_of_Space_Technology "China Academy of Space Technology").

On 6 December 2020 at 21:42 UTC, [Chang'e 5](/wiki/Chang%27e_5 "Chang'e 5") landed and collected the first lunar soil samples in over 40 years, and then [returned the samples](/wiki/Sample_return_mission "Sample return mission") to Earth. The 8.2t stack consisting of lander, ascender, orbiter and returner was launched to lunar orbit by a [Long March 5](/wiki/Long_March_5 "Long March 5") rocket on 24 November. The lander-ascender combination was separated with the orbiter and returner before landing near [Mons Rümker](/wiki/Mons_R%C3%BCmker "Mons Rümker") in [Oceanus Procellarum](/wiki/Oceanus_Procellarum "Oceanus Procellarum"). The ascender was later launched back to lunar orbit, carrying samples collected by the lander, and completed the first-ever robotic rendezvous and docking in lunar orbit.[[99]](#cite_note-99)[[100]](#cite_note-100) The sample container was then transferred to the returner, which successfully landed on [Inner Mongolia](/wiki/Inner_Mongolia "Inner Mongolia") on 16 December 2020, completing China's first extraterrestrial sample return mission.[[101]](#cite_note-101)

In Russia's first attempt to reach the Moon since 1976, and since the dissolution of the Soviet Union, the [Luna 25](/wiki/Luna_25 "Luna 25") spacecraft failed during "pre-landing" maneuvers, and crashed into the lunar surface on 19 August 2023.[[102]](#cite_note-102)

**Martin Meyerson** (November 14, 1922 – June 2, 2007)[[1]](#cite_note-NytMeyerson-1) was an American city planner, academic, and president of the [University of Pennsylvania](/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania") from 1970 to 1981. His research, mentorship, essays, and consulting were focused on post-[World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") [urban policy](/wiki/Urban_policy "Urban policy") at the municipal and federal levels.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Meyerson was born in [Brooklyn](/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"), New York City on June 2, 1922. He graduated from [Columbia University](/wiki/Columbia_University "Columbia University").[[3]](#cite_note-iht-3) He then obtained his [MA](/wiki/Master_of_Arts "Master of Arts") degree in city planning from [Harvard University](/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University").
